discussion_comments.comment_body: Bounded rather than removed in `5bb0e207e4`: `#rootCache` is cleared on every write (`#insertBatch`), so a repository created while the process runs is picked up at the next submission instead of after a restart (test: nested `git init`, then a write — `repo` scope for the outer repository empties and the inner one fills; it fails without the clear). Removing the cache outright measured ~2.5x slower per `repo` read (4.1 ms -> 10.5 ms on 14k rows / 370 directories), which is why the memoization stays. The false "a directory never changes repository mid-process" comment is gone. Residual: a topology change with no submission in between stays cached until the next write.

Valid, and fixed in `e0f1c62fee`. Reproduced with a second connection: an external writer inserting a row under an unseen subdirectory stayed invisible to `repo` scope, and a symlinked spelling of a known directory stayed invisible to `cwd` scope, until this process wrote.

`#dirsByTarget` now drops itself when `PRAGMA data_version` reports a foreign commit. That pragma moves only for other connections, so the unconditional clear in `#insertBatch` stays for our own writes, and the path-derived memos are left alone -- they describe the filesystem, not the row set.

Cost: ~1 us per scoped read versus ~0.37 ms to recompute the set on every read.

Test: `sees a row committed by another connection without a local write`, fails without the probe.

Residual, out of scope: a pure filesystem topology change by another process (a `git init`) with no database commit is still picked up only after a local write.

**blocking / maintainer call**: `PRAGMA data_version` does not change for commits on the same connection (SQLite docs: "unchanged for changes committed on the same database connection"). Beam is the only writer in the normal case, so this check almost never flushes the cache, and the module-level `embeddingCache` (line 604) only ever grows.

Probe on this head: I cached 3 ids, ran `DELETE FROM memory_embeddings; DELETE FROM working_memory` on the same `db`, and `data_version` stayed at `1 -> 1`. `getEmbeddingCacheStateForTests` still reported `size: 3`. Deleted or forgotten memories are never evicted.

The per-entry `cached.raw !== rawJson` check is what actually keeps results correct. But because of it, every entry holds the full raw JSON string *and* a parsed `number[]` for every id that `allVisibleIds` returns. That is the whole embedding table, about 2x its size, kept in the JS heap for the life of the process (roughly 40 KB per 1536-dim embedding). Every recall also still reads and compares every `embedding_json` string, so what this saves is the `JSON.parse` plus the norm computation.

Options:
- Key on a cheap fingerprint instead of keeping `raw`.
- Bound the cache or prune it to the ids returned by the current `allVisibleIds`.
- Keep it in `beam.caches` next to the existing query cache instead of a module-level `WeakMap<object, …>`.
- Reuse `databaseWriteToken()` (line 1284) if a coarse flush is wanted.

Also, #16994 adds a second embedding cache over the same table in `PolyphonicRecallEngine.vectorVoice`. Consider sharing one.

Not a defect — this is the trade the PR makes, and the current code already bounds it. The memo is a `WeakMap` keyed by the entry (`#entryLines` in session-manager.ts), so a cached line lives exactly as long as its entry: a pruned or released entry's line is collected with the entry, and nothing is retained beyond the live session. The retention the finding names is the same retention the reuse buys — the memo holds the serialized copy of a session the caller is already holding in memory, and the session file already holds those bytes on disk. A bound is not a free win here either: evicting a line requires holding the entry strongly enough to know it is gone, which keeps released entries alive — the opposite of what the finding asks for — and it would make the PR's own contract conditional ("rewrite only what changed" would hold only for a recent window). If the maintainer wants a ceiling anyway, the right shape is a byte-budgeted LRU over strong references, which is a separate design decision rather than a bug fix in this PR. We are leaving the WeakMap as it is.

+/**
+ * One entry's serialized line plus the state it was computed from, so a full
+ * rewrite re-serializes only the entries that changed.
+ *
+ * {@link #lineFor} projects the entry through `prepareEntryForPersistence`,
+ * which is a pure function of the entry's own **field values** — it strips
+ * replayed reasoning signatures, drops spilled MCP structured content,
+ * truncates oversized strings, and externalizes image payloads to
+ * content-addressed `blob:sha256:` refs (so the same payload always projects
+ * to the same ref). A line is therefore valid exactly while every field value
+ * it was derived from still holds, which the snapshots below check:
+ *

Fixed in f6c324020c. The hidden-classifier list is gone: the memo now gates on the carriers the atomic classification actually reads for the node's own brand (`atomicPersistenceCarrierKeys` in session-persistence.ts — `thinkingSignature`, `textSignature`, `thoughtSignature`, `encrypted_content`, `data`, `block`, and the typeless `anthropicCompaction` carrier's `content`), and a carrier the own-key stamp cannot see (inherited, own non-enumerable, or an accessor) leaves the graph uncached instead of letting the verdict flip under an equal stamp. Regression test: `persists the truncated text of a block whose hidden signature stops signing it` — a block whose `textSignature` is a non-enumerable own property is signed (its long text is persisted verbatim) until the signature is emptied, when the projector must truncate the text; on the previous head the stamp compared equal and the untruncated text was persisted, so the test failed with the full text still in the body. Checked with `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/entry-line-memo.test.ts` (60 pass / 0 fail).

**Blocking — branch navigation reuses a snapshot from the wrong branch.** This cache hit checks the session file, scope, and token but not the active branch. Repro: build/commit `Original`, let startup refresh build/commit `Rewritten`, then `sessionManager.branch(firstSnapshotId)`. `getBranchView()` now contains only `Original`, but this function still returns `Rewritten` from `memoryStateByTranscript`; a later process restores `Original` and changes the prompt again. Invalidate/reselect the cached state when the leaf moves outside its recorded snapshot's branch, and cover that transition.

Fixed in 99d4751f9f and e918bdb897: the staged state carries the branch anchor (`stagedLeafId`) and the snapshot is re-selected per branch, so a navigation off the recorded entry re-stages the block for the branch the user continued on. `test/memory-snapshot-resume.test.ts` covers the re-selection and the re-staging.
Fixed in 057fa9c7a1: the token is written with `Bun.write`, which creates the parent directory, so the separate `mkdir` is gone.

Already fixed in the current head: the working directory is part of the pool key (`packages/stats/src/aggregator.ts:283`) — a Bun worker keeps the cwd it was spawned under, so a moved cwd invalidates the pooled worker.

**should-fix (two mechanisms for one invariant).** `#liveEntriesMatch` already proves the cache is valid: same `start`, same length, and identical `entry` at every position. Since `index` is `start + offset`, that also covers every wrapper field. So the five `this.#liveWrappersStart = -1` invalidations (`removeChild` L365, `clear` L379-380, the offered-commit ack L996, the frontier advance L1393, `#syncEntries` L1623) never change the result; they only skip an O(n) compare that would fail anyway. Keep one mechanism. Dropping the manual resets keeps the cache correct by construction, so future mutations of `#entries`/`#frontier` can't forget to invalidate it. If you'd rather keep the resets as the contract, the per-entry loop is redundant instead. Also, the field doc (L310) says indexes stay valid "because entries are never spliced mid-frame", but correctness actually rests on the identity check.
